question: Should OpenClaw adopt this five-part localization series as a core cross-package runtime contract, including process-scoped CLI locale selection and the proposed shared package boundary?
rationale: The diff establishes new shared behavior across UI, onboarding, CLI, Gateway, and safety presentation; deciding the permanent locale, fallback, and ownership contract requires maintainer product and architecture intent beyond a mechanical patch review.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core foundation
options.body: Confirm the shared package and locale contract, require the release-owned changelog edit to be removed, and review the series one bounded dependency-aware slice at a time.

options.title: Keep localization surface-owned
options.body: Reject a new global runtime contract and retain independent locale handling until a smaller shared invariant is demonstrated.

options.title: Pause the series for RFC resolution
options.body: Wait for explicit RFC acceptance and owners for CLI, Control UI, Gateway, and channel presentation before accepting cumulative implementation work.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed core foundation
recommendation.body: Confirm the shared package and locale contract, require the release-owned changelog edit to be removed, and review the series one bounded dependency-aware slice at a time.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the identifiable author of the linked localization series and can clarify its intended boundary; final sponsorship remains a repository maintainer decision.
